source.note: results.json records client and service as the prefixes f12f779 and 5921064, which resolve uniquely here to these commits, reachable only from pre-rewrite development branches such as origin/adam/near-swap-complete-20260929; the service is the client's direct child. Both commits' Cargo.lock files resolve ipir-sp 0.1.0-rc.6 to ipir_sp, which results.json records only as 1f2aec65. These are source configuration: nothing records that the tested builds were clean checkouts of them. The protocol measured (q48) was replaced by this stack's pir-native protocol.

toolchain.status: unavailable: neither was recorded at the time
toolchain.note: The README's command passes no --profile, so as shown Cargo builds the test with its default test profile, but no record shows the command was run exactly as shown, nor how the isolated Enhance service was built. The client and service prefixes resolve in this repository's remote branches to commits whose rust-toolchain.toml pins Rust 1.91.0; a pin does not show what built. results.json's profile is the receiver PIR protocol profile (ironwood-receiver-pir-v1-q48, as in protocol here), not a Cargo profile.

host: Mac Studio (local, loopback) and the isolated Enhance integration service over SSH

each lookup's request and response at the historical q48 sizes at 8192 rows, as measured by this run's one query
derived.excludes: manifest, HTTP/TLS, Enhance, witness and spentness traffic, as for every receiver byte count in results.json
derived.note: A projection from one query's payload sizes, not traffic observed from fifty lookups.

whether the client and service builds were clean checkouts of the recorded commits (only 7-character prefixes were recorded at the time)

the exact commands executed; the README's command is the documented form

the RPC responses or checker output behind results.json's terminal-anchor validation; the anchor check cannot be re-verified from this run
